quote: Internet-based instruction provider Achieve3000 has received a $9 million investment from venture capital firm Insight Venture Partners in New York.
status_event: Acquired by McGraw Hill from Insight Partners, closed 1 November 2021.
notes: Entry was a $9M venture round in 2007 (panel: July 2007; reported 7 Aug 2007). Control came LATER: EdSurge 2018 says "In 2015, the company was acquired by private equity firm Insight Venture Partners." (https://www.edsurge.com/news/2018-10-02-achieve3000-acquires-literacy-startup-actively-learn). That matches the AC HoldCo, Inc. Form D (Delaware 2015, issuer at 1114 Avenue of the Americas, Insight people Blair Flicker, Eric Goldstein, Peter Sobiloff as directors, $233,961,508 sold, business combination = true, first sale 2015-03-18; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1637823/000089914015000363/0000899140-15-000363-index.htm). EdWeek 2018 calls Insight "a majority investor in Achieve3000"; Platinum Equity 2021: "Achieve3000, which was acquired from Insight Partners". So the owner evidence is real but describes the 2015 buyout, not the 2007 entry. The 2007 article does not use the word minority; the verdict rests on the $9M size plus the 2015 acquisition. HQ: EdWeek 2018 says Lakewood, N.J.; the dossier also names Red Bank, NJ.

quote: Parent company Appriss is a multibillion-dollar business owned by Clearlake and Insight Partners that licenses software on a subscription basis to public safety, risk and compliance, health information and insurance industries.
status_event: Appriss Health was renamed Bamboo Health in 2021 after buying PatientPing; the holding company still files Form D amendments with Insight and Clearlake directors (latest November 2025).
sources_checked: SEC Form D Alert Holding Company 2015-06-03 and 2016-06-03
SEC Form D Bamboo Health Holding Company 2023-11-02
notes: No source read states the 2014 stake size in words, so this is medium. Evidence for control at entry: (1) the first Form D of Alert Holding Company, Inc. (Delaware 2014, renamed Bamboo Health Holding Company in 2022; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1643449/000164344915000004/primary_doc.xml) lists four directors, three of them Insight people at 1114 Avenue of the Americas (Deven Parekh, Euan Menzies, Anika Agarwal) plus the CEO, and marks the offering as a business combination. The issuer address is the company's own in Louisville, so this is NOT the strict formd_vehicle pattern. (2) Appriss release Aug 2015 names Deven Parekh "chairman of the board for Appriss". (3) Bain Capital Ventures lists its Appriss holding as "Acquired". Evidence that leaves room for doubt: Clearlake release 2019: "With the investment, Clearlake will become an equal partner in Appriss alongside management and Insight Partners, which invested in Appriss in 2014." (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/appriss-to-receive-investment-from-clearlake-capital-to-continue-rapid-growth-and-expansion-300827879.html). Panel dates the entry November 2015; the Clearlake release dates Insight's entry 2014. The 2014 announcement itself was not found. Bizjournals articles returned 403.

quote: C/O INSIGHT VENTURE MANAGEMENT / 1114 AVENUE OF THE AMERICAS
status_event: Still an Insight portfolio company; raised a $35M Series B (equity from Insight plus venture debt) in November 2020 and bought StormForge in March 2025.
sources_checked: SEC Form D Cloudbolt Holdings 2018-08-03 (two filings) and D/A 2020-07-30
notes: SOURCES CONTRADICT. The quote is the issuer address field (street1 / street2) of the Form D. Cloudbolt Holdings, Inc. is a Delaware 2018 entity at Insight's address; Michael Triplett is "Director and President" and Thomas Krane "Director and Treasurer", both at 1114 Avenue of the Americas; the other two directors are CloudBolt executives (Brian Kelly CEO, Bill Schell). $31,992,820 sold, first sale 2018-06-01, business combination = true. That is the acquisition vehicle pattern, and $32.0M sold against a $23M announced round fits rollover equity. Against it: the company release says "today announced a $23M Series A funding round led by Insight Venture Partners" (https://www.insightpartners.com/ideas/cloudbolt-announces-23m-investment-from-insight-venture-partners-to-accelerate-growth-of-hybrid-cloud-management-platform/), and no press source read uses majority or acquisition. HQ: Rockville, MD in 2018; North Bethesda, MD dateline in November 2020.

quote: Insight Partners, which had previously backed Thycotic, remained involved in the combined company as a minority investor.
status_event: Formed in April 2021 when TPG merged Thycotic and Centrify; renamed Delinea in February 2022; owned by TPG.
notes: The verdict answers the row as the panel dates it (March 2021): a minority stake in the TPG-controlled combined company. If this row is merged with Thycotic, the entry is July 2015 and it is CONTROL: CRN 2021-03-02 says "Insight Partners has been Thycotic's majority owner since July 2015" (https://www.crn.com/news/security/tpg-capital-to-buy-thycotic-for-1-4b-merge-it-with-rival-centrify-report) and SiliconANGLE says "Thycotic is being purchased by TPG from majority owner Insight Partners". The 2015 release only says "a significant investment". Priced valuation of $1B or more: TPG agreed to buy Thycotic for $1.4 billion (CRN, 2021-03-02, reporting PE Hub). HQ from the Wikipedia infobox.

quote: Insight Partners alongside co-investor Farview will be joining historical majority shareholder, London-based private equity firm Livingbridge, who will be remaining as a minority shareholder to support Exclaimer's international expansion strategy.
status_event: Bought by an Insight-led group in December 2020 (over GBP 100M); still held through Origin Bidco Limited.
sources_checked: firm post 2020-12-07 (same text as the release)
UK Companies House: Exclaimer Group Limited PSC register, Origin Bidco Limited PSC register and officers, Origin Midco Limited PSC register
notes: The release says the former majority holder drops to a minority. The UK register confirms a change of control: Origin Bidco Limited (no. 13057211) became holder of 75% or more of the shares and votes of Exclaimer Group Limited on 30 December 2020, the day Livingbridge GP LP ceased (https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/10303952/persons-with-significant-control). Origin Bidco was set up on 2 December 2020 with Blair Flicker, Mark Lessing and Andrew Prodromos as first directors (Flicker is the Insight officer who signs AC HoldCo's Form D from Insight's address); Matthew Gatto and Henry Frankievich of Insight joined its board on 30 December 2020 (https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/13057211/officers). The chain runs Origin Bidco, Origin Midco, Origin Holdings Limited (Jersey), so the split between Insight and Farview is not visible.

quote: After private equity group Insight Venture Partners acquired a controlling stake in 2014, Frontline has gone on a shopping spree
status_event: Sold by Insight to Thoma Bravo in August 2017 at more than $1B; Thoma Bravo sold it to Roper Technologies in 2022 for $3.7B.
sources_checked: Blank Rome deal page (HTTP 429, title only)
notes: The quote is the opening clause of a longer sentence. Supporting: EdWeek 2022: "The private equity firm Thoma Bravo bought Frontline from Insight Venture Partners in August 2017 in a deal that valued the company at more than $1 billion." Thoma Bravo 2017: "Insight Venture Partners, a prior investor in Frontline, will retain a minority stake in the company." The 2014 release itself only says "a significant investment" with three Insight board seats. A Blank Rome page is titled "Frontline Technologies, Inc. Sells a Controlling Interest to Insight Venture Partners" but could not be read (429), so it is not quoted. Priced valuation of $1B or more: over $1B in August 2017 (https://marketbrief.edweek.org/strategy-operations/k-12-dealmaking-frontline-acquired-for-3-7b-illuminate-education-bought-by-renaissance/2022/08); $3.7B to Roper in 2022 (same article). HQ was Exton, PA at entry.

quote: Insight Venture Partners, a New York-based venture capital and private equity firm focused on software investing and majority owner of Illuminate and KDS, facilitated the combination.
sources_checked: SEC Form D Illuminate Education Holdings, Inc. 2014-12-02
SEC Form D Illuminate Education Holdings, LLC 2018-08-23
EDGAR filing lists for both CIKs
company release July 2018 (illuminateed.com, same text on llrpartners.com)
notes: SOURCES POINT BOTH WAYS. Majority ownership is proven only as of 2018: the company release above, and EdWeek 2018: "The private equity firm had the controlling interest in both KDS and Illuminate through a holding company just for them." EdWeek 2022 says the merged company "was formed by Insight Venture Partners in July 2018 through a mega-merger of five K-12 companies". The 2014 entry itself looks like a growth round: the Form D of Illuminate Education Holdings, Inc. (Delaware 2014, issuer at the company's Irvine address, signed by the company CFO) shows $26,500,000 sold to 6 investors, first sale 2014-11-21, business combination = false, and only one Insight person (Nikitas Koutoupes) among four directors (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1626301/000162630114000001/primary_doc.xml). The vehicle at Insight's own address, Education Software Technologies Holdings, LLC (renamed Illuminate Education Holdings, LLC), dates from 2017. Insight may have entered as a minority holder in 2014 and taken control by 2017. No source read states the 2014 stake. Treat as unclear if the owner-later rule is not enough.

quote: Jama sold a majority of the company to another investment firm, Insight Partners, as part of a $200 million recapitalization in 2018, though early backers Madrona Ventures and the Oregon Venture Fund had retained a stake.
status_event: Acquired by Francisco Partners for $1.2B, announced March 2024.
notes: The 2018 release words it as "a $200 million growth equity investment led by Insight Venture Partners with participation from Madrona Venture Group"; the press report names it a majority sale and a recapitalization. Priced valuation of $1B or more: $1.2B, 2024-03-18 (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/francisco-partners-to-acquire-jama-software-for-1-2b-302091992.html). Insight's January 2025 fund post lists the Jama sale among 2024 realizations, so the deal closed.

quote: today announced a strategic growth equity investment by global venture capital and private equity firm Insight Partners.
status_event: Still an Insight portfolio company; moved its headquarters to Boston in August 2021.
sources_checked: Lakeside release 2020-02-11 (own site and PR Newswire)
notes: No source read states majority or minority, and the amount was not disclosed (TechTarget: "The size of the investment from Insight Partners was not disclosed"). Signals that lean control but do not prove it: the company was self-funded until then ("has been self-funded up until now", TechTarget), two Insight people joined the board (Triplett, Frankievich), and a new CEO replaced the founder 18 months later (August 2021). The founder is again named as CEO in a February 2026 interview. HQ was Ann Arbor, MI at entry.

quote: The transaction still has to pass a regulatory review, but once complete, the current owners, Insight Venture Partners and Bessemer Venture Partners, will be bought out.
status_event: Sold by Insight and Bessemer to Permira funds in 2014; acquired by Quest Software in July 2018.
notes: Owner evidence only; the 2008 deal terms were not found. Control here is by the co-investor group (Insight with Bessemer). Willkie 2014: "Upon closing, Insight Venture Partners and Bessemer Venture Partners will fully exit their stakes in Metalogix." The article headline is "Metalogix bought by another private equity firm". A founder's page words the 2008 deal neutrally: "In 2008, Metalogix took investment from Bessemer and Insight Venture Partners". Permira's release says "Metalogix was founded in 2008", which fits a 2008 reorganisation around the new owners. Entry date is the panel's.

quote: Insight Partners will make a new equity investment into the combined company, rolling 100% of their Payfactors equity and joining Francisco Partners as part of the PayScale investor base.
status_event: Merged with Payfactors in March 2021; majority-owned by Francisco Partners since April 2019.
notes: The PayScale stake is a minority beside the controlling holder: GeekWire 2021-03-01: "The combined company will be majority-owned by private equity firm Francisco Partners" (https://www.geekwire.com/2021/payscale-payfactors-combine-600-person-company-eyeing-big-market-compensation-data/). On the judge's question: the stake DID come from Payfactors (rolled equity) plus new money. Insight's earlier entry into Payfactors was not found: no date, round or stake size in any source read; GeekWire says "Total prior funding for Payfactors was not disclosed." If the row becomes Payfactors, its entry verdict is unclear. Payfactors was based in the Boston area.

quote: today announced the close of a minority investment by global venture capital and private equity firm, Insight Venture Partners, alongside existing investor Georgian Partners.
status_event: Acquired by Q2 Holdings for $510M, closed around 31 October 2019.
notes: The release is dated 20 December 2017; the panel dates the first investment October 2017. Sale price from Finovate: "closed the books on a $510 million deal to purchase PrecisionLender".

quote: ThreatTrack Security Holdings, Inc. ("ThreatTrack Holdings") a Delaware holding [page break] company wholly owned by certain of our shareholders, including Insight, Bessemer Venture Partners and Greenspring, for a total purchase price of $27,000,000.
status_event: Renamed VIPRE and acquired by j2 Global in February 2018.
sources_checked: SEC Form F-1/A of GFI Software S.A. 2013-11-21
Form D records GFI Software in formd-sweep.json
notes: This is the citation the judge's note says is owed. The source is an SEC registration statement of the seller, GFI Software (evidence_kind has no filing value, so company_release is used). "[page break]" marks where the filing's page footer splits the sentence; the words are otherwise exact. Full context: in March 2013 GFI sold its subsidiary GFI Florida (the former Sunbelt Software) to ThreatTrack Holdings, a carve-out bought by a vehicle wholly owned by GFI's own shareholders. The same filing on the parent: "In May 2005, GFI Software LTD and its subsidiaries were indirectly acquired by GFI Acquisition Company Ltd., or "GFI Acquisition," an entity controlled by Insight, our majority shareholder." Insight's exact share of ThreatTrack Holdings is not stated. The panel dates the entry November 2013; the filing dates the sale March 2013. Status from Wikipedia (VIPRE), which cites CRN 2018-02-07.

quote: today announced the completion of a $53 million investment from Insight Venture Partners.
status_event: Merged with Exegy in May 2021 in a deal backed by Marlin Equity Partners.
sources_checked: Marlin & Associates pages (domain does not resolve, not read)
notes: No source read states majority or minority. The release is dated 9 January 2013; the panel dates the entry December 2012. Signals that lean control: $53M into a company founded in 2007, two Insight board seats, and the 2014 firm post calls Deven Parekh "chairman of board of directors of SR Labs" and says Insight "provided additional financing" for the Wombat purchase. A search result snippet from the seller's adviser (Marlin & Associates) spoke of existing shareholders keeping a significant stake in a recapitalized company, but the page could not be opened, so it is not quoted and not relied on. The 2021 merger sources do not name Insight as seller. The dossier's news headlines for this slug are about sailing yachts and an unrelated company, not this one.

quote: today announced it received a major investment from Insight Venture Partners.
status_event: Acquired by Euromoney Institutional Investor in 2019 for $20.4M in cash.
notes: The judge's note says the entry was reported as a majority; no source I could read says so. The release is titled "Wealth-X Raises Growth Capital From Insight Venture Partners To Accelerate Expansion", says the co-founders "will continue to lead the business", and gives Insight two board seats (Euan Menzies, Matthew Gatto). Fortune calls it a "multimillion dollar" investment. The 2019 sale sources that were reachable do not name the sellers. The release is dated 25 November 2014; the panel dates the entry September 2014. Sale price from BDO: "acquisition of Wealth-X Pte. Ltd for $20.4m in cash". HQ per the 2014 release ("Headquartered in Singapore").
